checks.label: A resultant vector results from adding two or more vectors together: on every ring the needle stands for all its pulls added, every chain runs nose to tail through the same pulls, and the resultant runs from the first tail to where the chain ends
Vectors cannot be added by simply adding their magnitudes: two equal pulls make a needle as long as their sizes added only when they point the same way, and a shorter one at every other angle
Two 3 kN pulls read 6, 4.24, 3 and 0 kN at 0°, 90°, 120° and 180°; the 90° and 120° puzzles answer 4.24 kN and 3 kN, and by parts the 120° pulls make 3 − 1.5 = 1.5 across and 2.6 up

Components can be added or subtracted separately: for pulls A and B the readout adds the across parts and the up parts on their own, the gathered parts end where the chain ends, and this holds wherever the nose of B is dragged
Either order reaches the same nose: B then A ends where A then B does, at 5i + 4j, and drawn together the two chains make a parallelogram whose diagonal from the shared tail is the resultant, 6.40 kN
The equilibrant has the same magnitude as the resultant but the opposite direction: added, it closes the chain and the needle reads zero; taken away, the gap and the needle come back
Three 3 kN pulls 120° apart close their chain into a triangle, so the needle reads 0 kN while their sizes add to 9 kN; changing any one pull opens the chain by exactly the change, along that rope
Every puzzle offers three different answers with exactly one accepted, gives each wrong one its own hint, and draws a wrong pick in red but a right one without
Before Check no puzzle's picture shows its answer, and a right answer shows it
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s
